title: Shop Now does not open the catalogue
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the home page.
Click SHOP NOW in the hero.
expected: The call to action opens the collection or another defined shopping destination.
actual: The URL and page remain unchanged; SHOP NOW is rendered as a paragraph without an action.
impact: The primary shopping invitation cannot be used.
remedy: Render a real link to /collection with a visible focus state.
retest: Mouse click and Enter on the focused link both open Collection.

title: Best Seller section has no products despite flagged catalogue items
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Allow the catalogue to finish loading.
Inspect BEST SELLER and compare the public product flags.
expected: Products marked bestSeller are displayed in the section.
actual: The section is empty although five catalogue records have bestSeller=true. The public bundle filters the different key bestseller.
impact: Merchandising content disappears and an empty section occupies the home page.
remedy: Use the product contract key bestSeller and map productName consistently. Add a populated-fixture component check.
retest: The five flagged records render with names and prices; an empty source has a deliberate empty state.

title: Latest Collection is not ordered by creation date
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the ten Latest Collection items.
Compare their createdAt values with the full public catalogue.
expected: A section labelled Latest Collection presents the newest products first, or explains its curation.
actual: The list takes the first ten API records. An October 14 record leads the list while newer October 22 records are available.
impact: The section title does not describe its actual selection.
remedy: Sort a copy of products by createdAt descending before taking ten, or rename the section Featured Collection.
retest: A fixture containing older and newer products displays the declared ordering.
note: Latest is an inferred merchandising criterion; confirm with the owner.

title: Reviews tab does not display reviews
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the product and allow its data to load.
Click Reviews (122).
expected: The selected tab displays the reviews or an honest unavailable state.
actual: The displayed content does not change; the tab is a paragraph without a click handler.
impact: Customers cannot inspect the reviews advertised by the page.
remedy: Implement accessible tabs backed by review data, or remove the inactive review tab and count.
retest: Selecting Reviews changes the panel; keyboard selection works and the empty state is truthful.

title: Product rating and review count are hard coded
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the cotton T-shirt.
Open the Women Zip-Front Jacket and compare the rating area with the public data and bundle.
expected: Rating and count derive from actual product reviews, or are clearly identified as sample content.
actual: Both display the same stars and (122); these values are fixed in the public component and not derived from review data.
impact: The storefront presents unsupported customer-feedback claims.
remedy: Aggregate approved reviews by product. Hide ratings when no verified review source exists; label demo fixtures explicitly.
retest: Products with zero, one and several reviews show the correct counts and calculated ratings.

title: Jacket description describes a short sleeved T-shirt
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open Women Zip-Front Relaxed Fit Jacket priced $399.
Read the short product description.
expected: The description explains the jacket actually offered.
actual: The jacket uses a generic round-neck, short-sleeved pullover shirt description. The same text is reused across different apparel types.
impact: Customers receive incorrect information about the item.
remedy: Replace copied descriptions with product-specific material, fit, closure and care details; validate catalogue content before publishing.
retest: Jackets, trousers and tops each have accurate descriptions matching their records and images.

title: Detailed Description panel explains ecommerce instead of the product
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the product.
Read the Description panel below the purchase controls.
expected: The panel contains useful details about this product.
actual: The text explains what an ecommerce website is rather than describing the selected apparel.
impact: A prominent information panel gives customers no product details.
remedy: Populate the panel from a product detail field; remove template instructional copy.
retest: Changing product changes the details and no ecommerce-definition template text remains.

title: Product image and title describe different garment styles
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open Men Round Neck Pure Cotton T-shirt priced $200.
Compare the main photo with the title and description.
expected: The images depict the named round-neck, short-sleeved T-shirt.
actual: The main photo depicts a pink collared, long-sleeved shirt while the title and description describe a round-neck T-shirt.
impact: The shopper cannot reliably determine which garment will be delivered.
remedy: Correct the product-to-image association or the product text after checking the intended inventory item.
retest: All gallery images match the approved product identity and garment characteristics.

title: Related Products includes the product already being viewed
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the $200 T-shirt.
Inspect Related Products.
expected: Recommendations provide other relevant items.
actual: The current product appears in its own related-product list; the filter does not exclude the current ID.
impact: A recommendation slot is wasted on an item already open.
remedy: Exclude the current product ID before limiting related results.
retest: No related result has the current ID, including after navigation between related items.

title: Selected size carries over when navigating to a related product
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Choose size M on the $200 T-shirt.
Open a related product priced $280.
Inspect the size selection before choosing a size again.
expected: The new product starts with no selection, or explicitly asks the customer to confirm its variant.
actual: M remains selected on the new product even though it was selected for the previous item.
impact: A shopper can add the next item using an unintended variant.
remedy: Reset variant and gallery state whenever productId changes; validate the selected size against the new product.
retest: Navigate between products with different size lists; adding requires a valid selection for the new item.

title: Unknown product leaves an incomplete purchase page
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the stated non-existent product ID.
Allow the request to complete.
expected: A Product not found state replaces purchase controls and offers a route back to the collection.
actual: The page shows an empty title, a currency symbol without a price, hard-coded review content and ADD TO CART.
impact: A broken URL looks like a purchasable item rather than a handled missing record.
remedy: Track loading, found, missing and failed states; render purchase controls only for a valid product.
retest: Missing and malformed IDs have a clear recovery page; valid products still load normally.

title: Search with no matches displays an unexplained empty grid
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open search on Collection.
Enter zzqa-no-such-product.
expected: A no-results message identifies the search and offers a clear or reset action.
actual: No product cards appear and no no-results explanation is displayed.
impact: Users cannot distinguish an empty result from a failed load.
remedy: Render a no-results state after loading completes, with a clear-search action.
retest: An impossible query shows the message; clearing it restores products.

title: Leading and trailing spaces prevent otherwise valid search matches
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Search for cotton.
Replace it with two leading spaces, cotton, and two trailing spaces.
expected: Incidental outside whitespace does not change the meaningful query.
actual: cotton finds 22 items, while the padded query finds none. The filter lowercases text but does not trim it.
impact: Pasted or casually typed queries produce false empty results.
remedy: Normalize the search with trim and consistent case handling before filtering.
retest: cotton, Cotton and padded cotton return the same matching IDs.

title: Collection filters and sorting are lost after returning from a product
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Select Men and Sort by Low to High.
Open a product.
Use browser Back.
expected: The previous collection criteria are restored.
actual: Men is unchecked and sorting returns to Relevant; all products are shown.
impact: Customers must repeat their selection after every product inspection.
remedy: Store search, category and sort criteria in URL parameters or durable route state.
retest: Back restores the same criteria and results, and a shared filtered URL opens the same view.

title: Footer navigation labels cannot be opened
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Go to the footer.
Attempt Home, About Us, Delivery and Privacy Policy.
expected: Each advertised navigation destination is an operable link.
actual: All four labels are static list items with no href or action.
impact: Customers cannot reach the pages promised by the footer.
remedy: Create valid links and publish the intended delivery and privacy content. Grouped here because the same footer implementation affects all four labels.
retest: All four destinations work with mouse and keyboard and have meaningful URLs.

title: Forgot your password has no recovery action
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the account form.
Click Forgot your password?
expected: A recovery flow or a clearly explained support alternative opens.
actual: The page stays unchanged; the text has a pointer cursor but no handler.
impact: A user who has forgotten a password has no advertised recovery path.
remedy: Implement a verified recovery process, or replace the inactive control with an accurate support instruction.
retest: The control opens recovery; account existence is not disclosed by recovery responses.

title: My Profile menu item has no destination
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Sign in with the disposable account.
Open the profile menu and click My Profile.
expected: The profile page opens or the unavailable feature is not presented as an action.
actual: No page or panel opens; My Profile is static text.
impact: The account menu advertises a function users cannot use.
remedy: Link to an implemented profile page or remove the inactive menu item until available.
retest: Selecting My Profile opens a working destination with the authenticated demo profile.

title: Explore Jobs does not open career information
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open Contact.
Click Explore Jobs.
expected: The button opens career details or a supported application destination.
actual: The page and URL remain unchanged.
impact: The careers call to action is nonfunctional.
remedy: Provide an actual careers link, or remove the button when no vacancies or careers page exist.
retest: Mouse and keyboard activation open the declared destination.

title: Newsletter subscription produces no result
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Enter a syntactically valid synthetic email in Subscribe now.
Click SUBSCRIBE.
expected: The form records the request and shows success or a useful error.
actual: There is no feedback or subscription action. The handler only prevents the default form submission.
impact: The advertised 20 percent offer has no usable subscription path.
remedy: Connect the form to the intended subscription service and show a result; remove the offer until its fulfilment works.
retest: Valid, duplicate and invalid requests produce truthful, accessible feedback without unintended subscriptions.

title: Product names are absent from cart and order rows
method: Browser test and public code review
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Add the $200 T-shirt in size M.
Inspect its cart row, then the own demo order history.
expected: Each row identifies the product by its stored productName.
actual: Images, price and size appear but the product name is blank. These views read name while records contain productName.
impact: Customers cannot clearly identify line items; the same data-contract mismatch affects both views.
remedy: Use one typed product contract and read productName in cart and order components.
retest: Names appear for all line items in both cart and order history.

title: Guest cart is overwritten after account creation
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: As a guest, add one item.
Create the disposable account.
Inspect the cart after authentication.
expected: The guest selection survives or is merged with the account cart.
actual: The badge changes from one item to zero and the guest item disappears when the empty account cart is loaded.
impact: A customer loses the prepared purchase at the authentication step.
remedy: Merge validated guest items with the account cart on authentication and reconcile the result before replacing local state.
retest: Guest-only and existing-account carts merge without loss or duplicate quantities.

title: An empty cart can be submitted as an order
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Use the authenticated demo account with an empty cart.
Proceed to checkout, complete the delivery form and submit cash on delivery.
expected: Checkout is blocked when there are no valid line items; the server rejects an empty items array.
actual: Order creation succeeds and the own-orders response contains an order with items=[] and amount=10.
impact: Invalid transactions are stored and can enter fulfilment workflows. Empty orders are also invisible in the flattened history.
remedy: Enforce non-empty validated items on the server and block the empty-cart checkout path in the UI.
retest: An empty order returns a validation error and creates no record; one valid item succeeds.

title: Empty-cart total does not agree with displayed shipping
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open an empty cart.
Compare Subtotal, Shipping Fee and Total.
expected: Displayed amounts reconcile, and no charge applies to an order that cannot be placed.
actual: Subtotal is $0.00 and shipping $10.00, but Total is $0.00. An empty submitted order instead stores $10.
impact: The stated payable amount is internally inconsistent.
remedy: Use one totals function across display and submission; hide or zero shipping for an empty cart.
retest: Empty and populated carts reconcile; submission and receipt equal the final displayed total.

title: Whitespace-only delivery information is accepted
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Enter three spaces in first name, last name, street, city, state and country; use a valid synthetic email.
Submit a demo COD order.
expected: Required address strings remain non-empty after trimming and are rejected otherwise.
actual: The order is accepted; the persisted address contains whitespace-only values.
impact: The stored order has no deliverable recipient or address.
remedy: Trim and validate required strings on both client and server; show errors beside the fields.
retest: Each whitespace-only required field rejects the order without persistence; a valid address succeeds.

title: Negative phone number is accepted at checkout
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Complete other delivery fields and enter -1 for Phone number.
Submit the authorized demo COD test order.
expected: The contact field accepts a valid telephone string and rejects an impossible negative number.
actual: The server stores phoneNumber="-1".
impact: The fulfilment team has no usable delivery contact.
remedy: Use type=tel and server-side phone validation appropriate to the supported countries; do not treat phone numbers as arithmetic quantities.
retest: -1 and malformed phones are rejected; supported formatted numbers remain intact.

title: Negative postal code is accepted at checkout
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Complete the other delivery fields and enter -1 for Zipcode.
Submit the authorized demo COD order.
expected: Postal codes are validated as country-appropriate identifiers.
actual: The persisted order contains zipCode="-1".
impact: The order can contain unusable delivery routing data.
remedy: Use a text postal-code field and validate it against the selected supported country on the server.
retest: Negative values fail; valid supported numeric and alphanumeric codes pass.

title: Order endpoint accepts a malformed delivery email
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Authenticate as the disposable account.
Submit one valid COD line item with address.email=not-an-email.
Fetch own orders.
expected: The server rejects a malformed email independently of browser validation.
actual: HTTP 200 success is returned and the malformed email persists in the order.
impact: API clients can create orders with unusable notification addresses.
remedy: Apply the same validated address schema at the API boundary; return a field-specific 4xx error.
retest: Malformed email creates no order; a valid synthetic email passes.

title: Order endpoint accepts a negative fractional quantity
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Use the demo account and a valid product ID.
Submit quantity=-0.5 in a COD order.
Read back own orders.
expected: Every apparel quantity is a positive integer within the allowed limit.
actual: The endpoint returns success and persists -0.5; the history displays that quantity.
impact: Invalid units corrupt order and fulfilment calculations.
remedy: Validate Number.isSafeInteger(quantity), quantity>=1 and a documented maximum before any write.
retest: -0.5, 0, fractional and excessive values fail; 1 and a valid upper bound pass.

title: Order endpoint accepts a size not sold for the product
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Submit the valid T-shirt ID with size=QA-NOT-A-SIZE.
Fetch the resulting own order.
expected: The chosen size belongs to the server-side product variant list.
actual: HTTP 200 success is returned and QA-NOT-A-SIZE is stored and displayed.
impact: The order requests an impossible product variant.
remedy: Resolve the product from the database and validate the requested variant against its current size list.
retest: Unknown sizes fail without persistence; supported sizes succeed.

title: Order endpoint accepts a non-existent product ID
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Submit item ID 000000000000000000000000 with a copied valid product snapshot.
Fetch own orders.
expected: Every order line references an existing saleable server-side product.
actual: The fabricated ID is accepted and persisted.
impact: An order can reference inventory that does not exist.
remedy: Look up every product and variant on the server; reject missing or unavailable records before writing the order.
retest: Non-existent IDs fail; existing allowed IDs succeed without trusting copied metadata.

title: Order endpoint trusts an altered client line-item price
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Copy the valid $200 T-shirt line.
Change its client price to 1 and submit amount=11.
Fetch own orders.
expected: The server uses its own catalogue price, ignoring a submitted client price.
actual: The order stores the altered $1 price and $11 amount.
impact: Price manipulation can create underpriced orders. No real payment or fraud was performed.
remedy: Accept only product ID, variant and quantity; derive immutable line prices and discounts from server rules.
retest: Tampered prices are rejected or ignored and the stored price remains $200.

title: Order endpoint trusts the submitted total amount
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Keep one valid line priced $200 with quantity 1.
Submit amount=1 rather than the displayed $210.
Fetch own orders.
expected: The server calculates the payable total from validated lines and shipping.
actual: The amount of 1 is persisted despite the unchanged $200 item.
impact: Totals can be manipulated independently of line-item prices.
remedy: Recalculate all monetary values on the server with an explicit currency and rounding policy.
retest: Altered totals cannot be stored; valid item $200 plus $10 shipping yields $210.

title: Cart endpoint stores a negative fractional quantity
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Use only the demo account cart.
Update an item quantity to -0.5.
Fetch the cart and reload its page.
expected: Cart quantities remain positive integers; removal uses an explicit operation.
actual: The update succeeds and -0.5 persists. The invalid fixture produced a fractional badge and negative totals.
impact: Cart arithmetic and checkout readiness become invalid.
remedy: Validate integer bounds server-side and sanitize existing invalid entries before computing totals.
retest: Invalid quantities fail and the cart remains unchanged; valid increments and removal still work.
note: Only the invalid demo entries created for this test were subsequently removed.

title: Cart endpoint accepts an unsupported size
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Authenticate as the disposable account.
Add the valid product with size=QA-NOT-A-SIZE.
Fetch its cart.
expected: The server rejects a variant not listed for that product.
actual: The unsupported size is stored in cartData.
impact: The cart holds a selection the storefront cannot legitimately fulfil.
remedy: Resolve the product variant before writing cart state and return a validation error for unknown sizes.
retest: Unsupported size is rejected with no cart change; valid size M is accepted.
note: The test entry was removed after evidence capture.

title: Cart endpoint accepts a non-existent product
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Add ID 000000000000000000000000, size M to the demo cart.
Fetch the cart and reload it.
expected: The cart accepts only existing saleable products.
actual: The fabricated ID is stored but cannot be resolved into a visible valid product row.
impact: Hidden invalid entries create inconsistent cart state and can break order construction.
remedy: Validate product existence on write and safely flag or remove stale references on read.
retest: Unknown IDs are rejected; deletion or unavailability of a previously valid product has a clear recovery state.
note: The fabricated test entry was removed after capture.

title: Guest checkout loses the address when authentication is required
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: As a guest with an item, complete the delivery form.
Press PLACE ORDER.
Follow the authentication flow.
expected: Authentication is requested before data entry, or the draft and checkout destination are preserved.
actual: Login is requested only on submission; the entered address is lost and successful signup returns to Home.
impact: A customer must repeat delivery entry and navigate back to checkout.
remedy: Guard checkout earlier or preserve a draft and returnTo destination across authentication.
retest: Guest-to-login and guest-to-signup flows return to checkout with the valid draft and cart intact.

title: Postal field strips letters from an alphanumeric code
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Type SW1A 1AA into Zipcode using normal keystrokes.
Read the resulting field value.
expected: A postal identifier is preserved for a supported destination; unsupported countries are explicitly excluded.
actual: The number input retains only 11 from SW1A 1AA. Country remains unrestricted free text.
impact: A legitimate alphanumeric postal code cannot be entered accurately.
remedy: Use type=text, preserve spaces and letters, and validate against the supported-country policy.
retest: SW1A 1AA is preserved when the UK is supported; otherwise the UI clearly restricts destination selection.
note: Supported-country requirements were not supplied; unrestricted country entry makes the current constraint ambiguous.

title: Phone field rejects a normally formatted telephone string
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Type +1 (415) 555-0321 into Phone number.
Inspect the resulting value.
expected: A telephone string can be entered and normalized without corrupting its meaning.
actual: The type=number control does not retain the entered formatted phone; the recorded value is empty.
impact: Customers cannot paste a commonly formatted contact number.
remedy: Use type=tel and appropriate inputmode, retaining the original string until validated and normalized.
retest: Formatted supported phone numbers work; invalid values receive a field-specific error.

title: Unknown route has no not-found message or recovery
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the stated unknown URL.
Allow the application to settle.
expected: A not-found view explains the invalid route and links to a valid destination.
actual: Only the shared header and footer appear; the route receives the SPA HTML with HTTP 200.
impact: Broken links leave users in an unexplained page and are difficult to diagnose.
remedy: Add a catch-all route with a clear message and recovery link; use an appropriate status when the hosting architecture permits.
retest: Unknown routes show Not found; known deep links still load on refresh.

title: Profile response includes password and refresh-token fields
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Sign in only as the disposable account.
Inspect the field names returned by the own-profile endpoint.
expected: The response contains only client-required profile data and excludes authentication internals.
actual: The field list includes password and refreshToken, as well as internal persistence metadata. Secret values were not copied into this report.
impact: Authentication material is unnecessarily exposed to client code. This is not evidence of access to other users.
remedy: Return an explicit safe profile DTO and exclude password hashes, refresh tokens and internal metadata from serialization.
retest: Own-profile and login responses omit these fields while authorised profile functions still work.

title: Search opener cannot be activated with the keyboard
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the search icon.
Traverse the header with Tab and attempt keyboard activation.
expected: The search opener is a named keyboard-operable button.
actual: The clickable image has no button role or tabindex and is absent from the normal interactive sequence.
impact: Keyboard-only shoppers cannot open search.
remedy: Use a button with an accessible name such as Open search, preserving the icon as decorative.
retest: Tab reaches the opener and Enter or Space opens the search form.

title: Search close icon lacks a keyboard action and name
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the search bar.
Inspect its close icon and try keyboard traversal.
expected: Close search is a named button reachable with Tab.
actual: The close affordance is a clickable image with empty alternative text and no button semantics.
impact: The visible closing action is unavailable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
remedy: Wrap the icon in a button labelled Close search and restore focus to the opener when it closes.
retest: The action is announced by name and closes the bar with Enter or Space.

title: Authenticated account menu is not keyboard operable
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Sign in and inspect the profile opener.
Inspect Orders and Logout in its menu.
expected: The opener and menu actions have suitable keyboard behaviour and semantic roles.
actual: The opener is a clickable div and image; menu actions are clickable paragraphs without normal keyboard semantics.
impact: Keyboard users cannot reliably open or use the account menu, including logout.
remedy: Use a named disclosure button, a link for Orders and a button for Logout with proper focus handling.
retest: The entire account menu can be opened, traversed, activated and dismissed using the keyboard.

title: Login and Create Account mode switch is not a keyboard control
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the account form.
Inspect and attempt keyboard activation of Login or Create Account.
expected: The mode switch is an operable button or link.
actual: The switch is a paragraph with an onClick handler and no keyboard control semantics.
impact: Keyboard users cannot select the alternative authentication form.
remedy: Use a type=button mode switch or links to explicit account routes.
retest: Enter and Space switch modes without submitting the form accidentally.

title: Product gallery thumbnails are pointer-only controls
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the product with multiple gallery images.
Inspect the thumbnail controls.
expected: Each thumbnail is keyboard operable and identifies the image it selects.
actual: Thumbnails are clickable images without button roles or tabindex.
impact: Keyboard shoppers cannot inspect alternative product views.
remedy: Use named buttons around thumbnails, exposing selected state and a visible focus indicator.
retest: All images can be selected using Tab and Enter; selected image state is announced.

title: Remove cart item is an unnamed pointer-only image
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Add one valid item.
Inspect the bin icon used to remove the row.
expected: Removal is a named keyboard-operable button identifying its item.
actual: The bin is an image click target without suitable alternative text or button semantics.
impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot reliably remove a line item.
remedy: Use a button labelled Remove [product name] with a clear focus style.
retest: The item is removable with the keyboard and focus moves to a sensible remaining control.

title: Cart product navigation is available only through a clickable image
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Add one item.
Inspect its image-based route to the product.
expected: An ordinary product link is available and identifies the destination.
actual: The image uses a click handler rather than an anchor; the visible product name is also blank.
impact: Keyboard users cannot use the cart shortcut back to product details.
remedy: Use an anchor containing an informative product name or image alternative.
retest: Tab reaches a named product link and Enter opens the correct product.

title: Mobile menu opener has no button semantics
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Use a 390 px viewport.
Inspect the menu icon.
expected: Open menu is a named button with its expanded state exposed.
actual: The visible opener is a clickable image without button semantics or aria-expanded.
impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users cannot reliably open mobile navigation.
remedy: Use a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls tied to the menu panel.
retest: Keyboard activation opens the menu and the announced state changes.

title: Mobile menu Back affordance is not keyboard operable
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open mobile navigation.
Inspect its Back image and text.
expected: The visible closing control is a keyboard-operable, named button.
actual: Back is implemented with a clickable div, image and paragraph rather than a button.
impact: A keyboard user lacks a reliable explicit close control.
remedy: Use a Close menu button and return focus to the original opener.
retest: Tab reaches Close menu; Enter or Space closes the panel and restores focus.

title: Closed mobile menu leaves offscreen links in the accessibility tree
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: At mobile width, close the menu.
Inspect the menu links and their hiding mechanism.
expected: Collapsed navigation content is removed from interactive and accessibility navigation.
actual: The panel is moved with translate-x-full; its links remain in the snapshot and are not inert or aria-hidden.
impact: Assistive navigation can expose offscreen destinations unrelated to the visible interface.
remedy: Conditionally mount the closed panel or use an appropriate inert/hidden state, restoring it when opened.
retest: Closed links are absent from the accessibility and tab sequence; opening makes them available.
note: The observed accessibility-tree exposure is confirmed; individual assistive-technology behaviour was not separately tested.

title: Mobile menu does not manage focus or dismiss on Escape
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the mobile menu.
Press Escape while a navigation item is focused.
Inspect focus handling.
expected: An overlay menu provides predictable focus and dismissal behaviour.
actual: Escape leaves the menu open; no opening focus transfer or closing focus restoration is implemented.
impact: Keyboard users can lose their position in navigation.
remedy: Choose a disclosure or dialog interaction model and implement its focus and Escape behaviour consistently.
retest: Open, traverse, Escape and reopen the menu; focus remains predictable throughout.

title: Mobile filter disclosure is a paragraph rather than a control
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Use mobile Collection.
Inspect the FILTERS toggle.
expected: A button opens filters and exposes expanded or collapsed state.
actual: The toggle is a clickable paragraph without button semantics or expanded-state metadata.
impact: Keyboard and assistive users cannot reliably discover and operate filtering.
remedy: Use a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls for the filter group.
retest: Keyboard opening works and the state is announced correctly.

title: Payment methods are not keyboard selectable radio controls
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Open checkout.
Traverse to the Stripe and Cash on Delivery choices.
expected: Payment methods form a labelled radio group with keyboard selection and selected-state exposure.
actual: The choices are clickable divs and decorative circles, with no radio or button semantics.
impact: Keyboard customers cannot select a payment method reliably.
remedy: Use labelled radio inputs in a fieldset and expose the selected payment option.
retest: Tab and arrow keys select each method; the selected method is announced.

title: Stripe option has no accessible payment-provider name
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect the Stripe choice in the checkout accessibility snapshot.
expected: The provider name Stripe is available as text or an accessible label.
actual: Only a logo with alt="" appears; the option has no text label and is absent as a named choice.
impact: A screen-reader user cannot identify this visible payment option.
remedy: Add the text label Stripe to its radio option; retain the logo as decorative.
retest: The provider is announced as Stripe together with its selected state.
note: This checks the accessible name, separately from the keyboard-selection defect.

title: Selected product size is communicated only by colour
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Select size M.
Inspect its button attributes before and after selection.
expected: The selected variant has a programmatically exposed state.
actual: Only the border/background classes change; no aria-pressed or radio checked state indicates the selected size.
impact: Assistive users cannot determine which size will be added.
remedy: Use a labelled size radio group, or expose aria-pressed consistently on selection buttons.
retest: Selecting M announces its state and clears the previous selection.

title: Collection sort selector has no associated label
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the sort select element and its labels or aria-label.
expected: The control has a programmatic label explaining its purpose.
actual: The select has no label, id association or aria-label; only option text contains Sort by.
impact: The control purpose depends on selected option text rather than a stable accessible name.
remedy: Associate a Sort products label with the select.
retest: The control is announced by its purpose with each available option.

title: Delivery fields rely on disappearing placeholders
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect delivery inputs before entry.
Type values into first name, address and contact fields.
expected: Persistent visible labels identify the fields after entry and provide programmatic associations.
actual: There are no associated labels; placeholders disappear as values are entered. Numeric postal and phone controls appear unnamed in the snapshot.
impact: Customers lose field context and assistive users encounter unnamed controls.
remedy: Add label elements linked to stable input IDs for every delivery field; keep placeholders as optional examples.
retest: All nine fields retain visible and accessible names after entry.

title: Authentication fields have no persistent associated labels
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open Signup or Login.
Fill username, email and password and inspect labels.
expected: Each credential field retains a visible label and programmatic association.
actual: Only placeholders identify the fields; no label associations are present.
impact: Entered forms lose clear visual context and depend on placeholder interpretation.
remedy: Add associated Username, Email and Password labels to the account form.
retest: Both modes keep field names visible and expose them correctly after entry.

title: Personal-data inputs do not expose their autocomplete purposes
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect autocomplete attributes on delivery name, address, email and phone inputs.
expected: Known personal-data purposes are exposed using appropriate autocomplete tokens.
actual: The fields do not specify purpose tokens such as given-name, street-address, postal-code or tel.
impact: Assistive personalization and reliable browser autofill lack explicit field-purpose metadata.
remedy: Add correct autocomplete tokens for each supported personal-data field and authentication mode.
retest: Inspect the corrected DOM and verify a test autofill preserves each field purpose.

title: Muted home-page text has insufficient contrast
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect policy and newsletter text rendered in gray-400 on white.
Calculate contrast from the observed computed colour.
expected: Normal-size text meets a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
actual: The computed colour is oklch(0.707 0.022 261.325) at 16 px on white, approximately RGB [153, 161, 175]. The calculated contrast ratio is 2.60:1, below 4.5:1.
impact: Low-vision users may struggle to read service-policy and newsletter text.
remedy: Use a darker approved text colour and check all states against the real background.
retest: The same text at 16 px measures at least 4.5:1 without relying on rounding.
note: The exact converted sRGB colour and ratio are included in the evidence summary.

title: Newsletter input suppresses its visible keyboard focus
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Focus SUBSCRIBE, then Shift+Tab into the email input.
Inspect the focus outline and screenshot.
expected: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on the input.
actual: The input uses outline-none and no focus shadow; the observed focus has no visible outline or replacement.
impact: Keyboard users cannot easily locate the active subscription field.
remedy: Provide a distinct focus-visible border or outline with sufficient contrast.
retest: Tab and Shift+Tab clearly indicate focus without requiring pointer interaction.

title: Meaningful product photographs have empty alternative text
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the main product image and gallery alternatives.
expected: Meaningful product views have concise text alternatives describing the item or view.
actual: The product images use alt="" despite conveying garment identity and appearance.
impact: Screen-reader users cannot obtain information conveyed by the product photography.
remedy: Provide accurate item and view alternatives; use empty alt only for genuinely decorative or fully redundant images.
retest: The main image and each informative gallery view expose useful, non-duplicative alternatives.

title: Visible page and section titles are not semantic headings
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect Collection, Cart, Checkout, About and Contact heading outlines.
expected: Page titles and major sections use a logical h1-h2 hierarchy.
actual: The inspected pages have paragraph-based titles and no h1-h3 outline; the common title component renders a p.
impact: Assistive heading navigation cannot follow the visible document structure.
remedy: Use semantic headings in the shared title component with context-appropriate levels.
retest: Every page has a meaningful h1 and logical section headings without skipped structural levels.

title: Page content lacks main and footer landmarks
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect document landmarks on Home and Collection.
expected: Main content and the site footer have suitable landmark semantics.
actual: No main or contentinfo/footer landmarks are present; major regions are generic containers.
impact: Assistive users have fewer efficient ways to navigate page regions.
remedy: Use one main element per page and a footer for shared closing content.
retest: Landmark navigation identifies Navigation, Main and Content information in a sensible order.

title: Browser title does not identify the current page
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Navigate between Home, Collection, Product, About and Checkout.
Compare document.title.
expected: Each title describes its page purpose and the store.
actual: All inspected routes retain Forever Mart.
impact: Tabs and assistive page announcements do not distinguish destinations.
remedy: Set route-specific titles such as Collection | ForeverMart and include product names on detail pages.
retest: Each route and direct deep link exposes an accurate title.

title: Layout overflows horizontally at 320 CSS pixels
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Set the viewport to 320 CSS px.
Inspect the header and checkout document width.
expected: The page reflows without horizontal scrolling for ordinary content.
actual: At 320 CSS px, the settled checkout document and body are both 352 px wide. The totals panel uses min-w-80 within the page margins.
impact: Small-screen and zoomed users must pan horizontally to reach content.
remedy: Remove fixed minimum widths that exceed the available content area; wrap header controls and stacked form panels.
retest: At 320 CSS px, document width is no greater than the viewport and all controls remain usable.
note: Reproduced again at the stated viewport; a screenshot and the full DOM snapshot are retained.

title: Home-page hero misspells Arrivals
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open Home and read the hero heading.
expected: The heading reads Latest Arrivals.
actual: The visible heading reads Latest Arivals.
impact: The first impression contains a spelling mistake.
remedy: Correct the copy and add a content proofreading checklist.
retest: The rendered heading and accessible heading text both read Latest Arrivals.

title: Template filler text remains in customer-facing sections
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Read the home collection descriptions, newsletter copy and footer.
expected: Public copy explains the store and each section.
actual: Several visible paragraphs contain Lorem ipsum template text.
impact: Customers see unfinished content instead of useful information.
remedy: Replace all placeholder paragraphs with approved store copy and search the production content for template text.
retest: No Lorem ipsum remains on public routes; reviewed copy is meaningful.

title: Contact details conflict between the footer and Contact page
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Compare Contact page details with its footer.
expected: The store publishes one verified contact set, or clearly labels different departments.
actual: The footer shows +1-212-444-780 and contact@foreveryou.com; Contact shows (415) 555-0321 and admin@forever.com without an explanation.
impact: Customers do not know which contact details belong to the store.
remedy: Centralize approved contact data and label any distinct support or administrative contacts.
retest: Each route shows the same approved support contact or explains the difference.

title: About page contains an incomplete support sentence
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Read the support paragraph on About.
expected: The sentence is complete and understandable.
actual: The copy ends with assist you the way, leaving the intended meaning incomplete.
impact: The About page communicates unfinished copy.
remedy: Rewrite the sentence and proofread the complete About page.
retest: The paragraph is grammatically complete and approved by the content owner.

title: Winterwear filter has no matching catalogue classification
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Select winterwear and compare the public subCategory values.
expected: Filter options reflect available classifications or explain an empty category.
actual: winterwear returns an empty grid; the catalogue uses only Topwear and Bottomwear, including for jackets.
impact: An apparently useful filter has no compatible records.
remedy: Align the taxonomy and product classification, or omit unavailable options until they contain products.
retest: Every advertised filter is backed by the intended classification or has an explicit empty state.
note: The intended garment taxonomy requires owner confirmation.

title: Empty cart has no explanatory state or shopping recovery
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Open the cart with zero items.
expected: The page states that the cart is empty and offers a clear shopping action.
actual: There are no rows or empty-cart explanation, but checkout remains the main action.
impact: Customers receive little guidance when nothing is selected.
remedy: Add an empty-cart message and a Continue shopping link; suppress checkout in that state.
retest: A new or cleared cart has a clear recovery action.

title: Checkout does not show the products being purchased
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Open checkout after adding a valid item.
Inspect the review information.
expected: A shopper can verify product, variant and quantity before submission.
actual: Only monetary totals and address fields are shown; no item summary is presented.
impact: The final screen does not help customers catch selection mistakes.
remedy: Include a concise order summary with item names, quantities, sizes and prices, with an edit-cart link.
retest: The summary agrees with the cart and server-calculated final order.

title: Order history omits order identifiers
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Open own demo order history and compare it with the own-orders API.
expected: Customers have a visible order reference for support.
actual: The API has order IDs, but the interface does not display them.
impact: A customer cannot cite an unambiguous order reference from the interface.
remedy: Show a safe order reference on each order group and use it in support or detail links.
retest: Each displayed order has a unique visible reference matching its record.

title: Order history loses order-level grouping
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect the own order history and the public order-view component.
expected: Line items are grouped under the order that owns them.
actual: The component pushes all order items into one list and renders item rows without order containers.
impact: Customers cannot clearly distinguish separate purchases with similar items.
remedy: Render order-level sections containing their line items, reference, date and total.
retest: Two orders and a multi-item order are visually distinguishable; empty invalid records are not silently hidden.
note: The flattening implementation was inspected; a multi-item-order scenario was not executed.

title: Order history omits the final order total and shipping breakdown
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect the order priced $210 in the own-orders data and its visible row.
expected: The customer can verify the stored final payable amount.
actual: Only item price and quantity are shown; the stored order total and shipping breakdown are not displayed.
impact: The view cannot serve as a complete order cost confirmation.
remedy: Show order subtotal, shipping, discounts where applicable, currency and final total from the validated order record.
retest: The $200 test item plus $10 shipping displays a $210 final total.

title: Order history has no delivery-address review
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Open own order history after the test order.
Inspect the delivery information available to the customer.
expected: An order detail view allows the customer to review the submitted delivery address safely.
actual: The visible history provides no address or detail link for reviewing it.
impact: A delivery-entry mistake cannot be checked from the current customer interface.
remedy: Provide an authenticated order-detail view with the delivery address and contact information.
retest: Own order details show the stored address; another account cannot retrieve it.

title: About page advertises product ranges absent from the inspected catalogue
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Read the advertised product ranges.
Compare with the 40 returned product records.
expected: Marketing copy reflects the current offer or explicitly describes future ranges.
actual: About mentions electronics, beauty and home essentials while the inspected catalogue contains apparel only.
impact: The current copy can create expectations the store does not presently meet.
remedy: Align copy with the current catalogue or label future expansion clearly.
retest: Each current-range claim is supported by published products.

title: Newsletter placeholder contains incorrect wording
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the newsletter email placeholder.
expected: The field instruction is clear and correctly written.
actual: The placeholder reads enter you email.
impact: A visible entry instruction contains a grammar error.
remedy: Use a persistent Email address label and an optional example placeholder.
retest: The form contains clear approved wording before and after entry.

title: Copyright footer contains incomplete grammar and inconsistent branding
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Read the copyright footer and compare its named domain with the store identity.
expected: The notice is correctly written and uses the approved store or legal-owner identity.
actual: The line reads Copyright 2025@ forever.com -All Right Reserved.; the store is presented as Forever Mart.
impact: The footer appears unfinished and its ownership identity needs clarification.
remedy: Use the approved legal identity and All rights reserved wording. Verify the year policy rather than automatically replacing it.
retest: The notice is grammatically correct and its owner is approved.
note: A 2025 year is not itself classified as a defect; it may identify the original publication year.

title: Public document has no Content Security Policy
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the saved response headers and public HTML head.
expected: A production hardening policy limits script and other resource sources as appropriate to this app.
actual: Neither a Content-Security-Policy response header nor a CSP meta policy is present in the inspected document.
impact: The page lacks this defence-in-depth control; no script-injection exploit was demonstrated.
remedy: Develop a least-privilege CSP using report-only validation before enforcing it, including the actual API, image and payment dependencies.
retest: The reviewed policy is present and all authorised app flows work without unexpected violations.

title: Public document lacks an explicit framing restriction
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect frame-related response headers and policy directives.
expected: The deployment restricts embedding to explicitly approved origins.
actual: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors restriction is present in the inspected response.
impact: Clickjacking defence is not configured in this response; an exploit was not attempted.
remedy: Set a suitable CSP frame-ancestors policy and, where appropriate, X-Frame-Options for older clients.
retest: An unauthorised framing origin is blocked and approved integrations continue to work.

title: Public responses omit the nosniff hardening header
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect X-Content-Type-Options in the saved public response.
expected: Responses use correct content types and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
actual: The inspected response contains no X-Content-Type-Options header.
impact: An additional browser MIME-sniffing defence is absent; no MIME-confusion exploit was demonstrated.
remedy: Configure nosniff consistently and verify asset MIME types.
retest: HTML, script, stylesheet and image responses have correct types and the intended header.

title: Public document has no explicit Referrer Policy
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect Referrer-Policy headers and meta tags in the document.
expected: The application explicitly defines the referrer information it permits external destinations to receive.
actual: No explicit policy is present; browser defaults determine behaviour.
impact: The deployment leaves this privacy setting implicit; this finding does not claim a proven data leak.
remedy: Choose and configure an appropriate policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin after reviewing navigation needs.
retest: Inspect same-origin and cross-origin navigation to confirm the intended information is sent.

title: Offscreen catalogue images are not marked for lazy loading
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Load the 40-product collection.
Inspect loading attributes on product images below the fold.
expected: Non-critical offscreen images can defer loading while initial visible content remains prioritised.
actual: The inspected image elements have no loading=lazy attribute.
impact: The implementation misses a possible transfer-saving optimisation; no Core Web Vitals failure is claimed.
remedy: Lazy-load offscreen cards, keep initial visible images eager, and measure the impact on a representative device.
retest: A network trace verifies deferred offscreen requests without delaying visible products.

title: Product images do not advertise responsive source variants
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect catalogue image srcset and sizes attributes at desktop and mobile widths.
expected: Image delivery can select a suitably sized source for the rendered card.
actual: The inspected images use a single source with no srcset or sizes attributes.
impact: Smaller screens cannot request a deliberately smaller variant through these attributes; actual speed impact was not measured.
remedy: Generate appropriate Cloudinary or equivalent variants and declare sizes and srcset.
retest: Mobile and desktop request suitable image dimensions while retaining image quality.

title: Public pages lack a page-specific meta description
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect the document head and route title updates.
expected: Indexable store pages provide concise, page-specific descriptive metadata.
actual: The inspected HTML has no meta description and the client does not populate a route-specific description.
impact: Search and sharing systems have little authored summary information. This is an optimisation observation.
remedy: Add approved descriptions for indexable routes and product pages using a route-aware metadata strategy.
retest: Rendered page heads contain distinct relevant descriptions without indexing private account routes.

title: Footer email and telephone cannot be activated directly
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Inspect and click the email and telephone strings in the footer and contact details.
expected: Customers can activate an approved support email or phone link on compatible devices.
actual: The details are static text without mailto or tel links.
impact: Customers must manually copy contact information, especially awkward on phones.
remedy: After approving the contact values, provide mailto and tel links with meaningful accessible names.
retest: The links invoke the corresponding device action without sending a message automatically.

title: Checkout does not state which dollar currency is used
preconditions: Authenticated disposable demo account; cash on delivery; no real payment.
steps: Inspect the displayed prices and final checkout total.
expected: The payable amount identifies its currency unambiguously.
actual: Only $ is shown; no ISO currency label is displayed while the country field is unrestricted.
impact: An international customer cannot distinguish USD from other dollar currencies from the checkout display.
remedy: Display the actual supported ISO currency next to the final total and align the payment configuration.
retest: Cart, checkout and order confirmation use one consistent, explicit currency.

title: Displayed return and exchange promises lack instructions
preconditions: Public deployment available; use the stated page and test data.
steps: Read Easy Exchange Policy and 7 Days Return Policy.
Look for a working route to the policy details.
expected: Customers can read the scope, conditions and procedure behind these service promises.
actual: The promises are brief text only; the inspected interface provides no usable policy-detail route or procedure.
impact: Customers cannot determine how to request the promised service.
remedy: Publish owner-approved policy details and link directly from the service summary.
retest: A customer can find eligibility, timeframe, procedure and support contact from each summary.
